sections.d: อ่านบทความแล้วตอบคำถาม 9 ข้อ (ข้อ 13–21)

p.t: How a Swarm Chooses a Home
x: In late spring a honeybee colony that has grown too large for its cavity divides. The old queen leaves with perhaps ten thousand workers and the swarm settles on a branch as a hanging cluster, where it may remain for two or three days. It is a dangerous interval. The bees carry only the honey in their stomachs, they have no comb and no shelter, and yet within that window they must select a new home. The decision is not made by the queen, who takes no part in it at all, and it is not made by a majority of the cluster, most of which never leaves the branch.

The work is done by a few hundred experienced foragers acting as scouts. Each flies out alone, and any scout that finds a possible cavity inspects it thoroughly, walking over the inner surfaces and making short flights around the entrance for as long as an hour. A scout that is impressed returns to the cluster and performs the same waggle dance that bees use to advertise flowers, with one crucial difference: the length of the dance reflects how good the site is. A superb cavity may be advertised for a hundred circuits, a mediocre one for a dozen, and a poor one not at all. Other idle scouts follow the directions, inspect the site for themselves, and dance on their own assessment rather than repeating what they were told.

Because enthusiasm is proportional to quality, the better sites gather supporters faster, while dances for weaker sites fade as their advertisers lose interest and stop. Crucially, no scout keeps dancing indefinitely; each gradually reduces its display and falls silent. This decay prevents the swarm from locking on to the first cavity anyone happens to find. When the number of scouts gathered at one site passes a threshold of roughly fifteen or twenty, the scouts return and begin producing a high-pitched signal that warms the cluster for flight, and the swarm lifts off — often before most of its members have any information about where they are going.

Researchers who tested the process on an island with no natural cavities, offering boxes of measured quality, found that swarms chose the best available box in the great majority of trials. What interests engineers is that this accuracy is achieved without any bee comparing the options. No individual visits more than one or two sites, and none holds a ranking in its head; the comparison happens in the pattern of dances, not in any bee's mind. Attempts to copy the mechanism in networks of simple machines have had mixed results, largely because the artificial versions tend to leave out the least obvious ingredient — the steady fading of enthusiasm that keeps the group from committing too early.

sections.d: อ่านบทความแล้วตอบคำถาม 9 ข้อ (ข้อ 22–30)

x: Few environmental habits are as widely praised as recycling. It is visible, it feels productive, and it asks very little of the household beyond sorting. Yet the industry that receives the sorted material works under constraints that are rarely explained to the people filling the bins. A recycling plant is a business that must sell what it collects, and the price of its products is set by markets for new material. When the price of crude oil falls, new plastic becomes cheap, and the bales of used plastic in the yard become almost worthless overnight.

The physical limits are just as important as the financial ones. Glass and most metals can in principle be melted and reformed without any loss of quality, which is why aluminium cans are collected almost everywhere at a profit. Paper fibres, by contrast, become shorter each time they are pulped, so office paper descends through a sequence of lower-grade products until the fibre is too short to bind. Most plastics behave worse still, because the polymers degrade and because there are dozens of incompatible types; a batch contaminated with the wrong resin produces a brittle product that no manufacturer will buy. For these materials, recycling delays disposal rather than preventing it.

Contamination is the difficulty that plant managers mention first. A greasy pizza box, a bottle with liquid still in it, or a plastic bag wrapped around the machinery can spoil a whole load or halt a sorting line. For years exporting the problem was the standard answer: mixed material was shipped abroad for hand sorting in countries where labour was cheap. That arrangement ended abruptly in 2018, when China refused to accept most imported waste. Prices collapsed, several municipal programmes in wealthy countries were suspended, and the uncomfortable fact became visible that a good deal of carefully sorted household material had never been recycled at all.

None of this argues for abandoning the bins; aluminium, glass and clean cardboard remain genuine successes. But it does suggest that recycling has been allowed to occupy space in public attention out of proportion to what it can achieve. Studies of household environmental behaviour repeatedly find the same pattern: people who recycle diligently often believe they have done their share, and are then no more likely than anyone else to reduce what they consume in the first place. Some researchers argue that the promotion of recycling by packaging manufacturers, beginning in the 1970s, was never innocent, since a habit that places responsibility on the consumer is a comfortable alternative to redesigning the product.

items.ex: ตอบข้อ 2 — ย่อหน้า 3 ยกตัวอย่างการปนเปื้อน กล่องพิซซ่าเปื้อนมัน ขวดที่มีน้ำเหลือ หรือถุงพลาสติกพันเครื่องจักร ว่าทำให้ทั้งล็อตเสียหรือทำให้สายคัดแยกหยุดได้ · ข้อ 1, 3 และ 4 กลับความหมายของตัวอย่างนี้

items.ex: ตอบข้อ 3 — ย่อหน้า 3 ระบุว่าเมื่อจีนปฏิเสธรับขยะนำเข้าส่วนใหญ่ ราคาก็ทรุด และโปรแกรมของเทศบาลหลายแห่งในประเทศร่ำรวยถูกระงับ · ข้อ 1 กลับทิศ · ข้อ 2 และ 4 บทความไม่ได้กล่าวถึงเป็นผลของเหตุการณ์นี้
